newsitem.title: czech republic: Czech PX50 slumps led by Wall St. and crown fears.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 slumps led by Wall St. and crown fears.

text.p: Czech shares fell sharply at Tuesday's fixing on the Prague bourse led by heavy losses in overnight trading on Wall Street and worries among investors that the Czech crown may face further depreciation pressure.

"It's something to do with Wall Street but foreign investors still think the crown may go slightly lower and maybe expectation of this is creating room for the falls," said Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka.
The PX50 fell 1.16 percent led by the major issues. SPT Telecom dropped 48 crowns to 3,327 and power utiliuty CEZ fell 19 crowns to 881.
The crown has held steady since the central bank was forced to float it after coming under sustained speculative pressure at the end of May.

On Monday the Czech Statistical Bureau released better than expected foreign trade figures for May but analysts warned that the expectation of falling interest rates would probably cancel out any boost to the crown from the lower trade deficit.
The central bank has so far left its discount rate, currently 13 percent, and its Lombard rate, 50 percent, unchanged. But its has been gradually cutting short term repo rates.
